summary: Implementation is correct and complete. Both call sites correctly use self._cached_slim_val (the preserved slimmed val df) instead of self._train_df. The defensive None guard is properly placed before the gate logic at both sites. The deviation from self._scoped_val_df to self._cached_slim_val is correct: _scoped_val_df is freed to None at line 2365 during __init__, while _cached_slim_val persists across park/unpark cycles. slim_backtest_df preserves all required columns (META_COLUMNS including datetime, LABEL_COLUMNS, _symbol_bar_index). All 3 new tests pass and exercise meaningful scenarios. All 221 tests across 4 suites pass.

findings.title: Missing code comment explaining _cached_slim_val deviation from _scoped_val_df
findings.description: The task spec originally called for using self._scoped_val_df, but the implementer (correctly) used self._cached_slim_val because _scoped_val_df is freed to None at line 2365. This rationale exists only in the implementer/spec-reviewer handoffs, not in the code. A future maintainer may not understand why _cached_slim_val is used instead of _scoped_val_df and could attempt to 'fix' it back.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief comment at one or both call sites, e.g.: '# Uses _cached_slim_val because _scoped_val_df is freed to None after __init__; _cached_slim_val is the preserved slimmed copy.'

findings.title: Fragile test construction via object.__new__
findings.description: Test builds Rule_Pool_Generator via object.__new__ + ~20 manual attribute assignments to bypass __init__ side effects. If __init__ adds or renames a required attribute, this test will break in confusing ways unrelated to the gate behavior.
findings.recommendation: Consider creating the generator via __init__ with val_df=None and using monkeypatch to skip _build_engines side effects, or simply patching _build_engines to a no-op before __init__ runs. This would make the test more resilient to future __init__ changes.

findings.title: Second call site comment is more terse than the first
findings.description: The first call site (~line 2830) has a detailed comment explaining the OOS stability check rationale and 'val split'. The second call site (~line 3320) only says 'Monthly-window gate for islands' followed by the audit fix comment. While this was pre-existing, making both comments consistently describe the val-split usage would improve maintainability.
findings.recommendation: Sync the second call site comment to mention 'val split (OOS stability check)' like the first.
